title: Show HN: Let's Seal – Let's Encrypt for document signing, free and self-hosted
body:
TLDR, Let's Seal gives the finger to Adobe and every doc signing tool (docusign, google, etc) who pay to play with the Adobe Approved Trust List and then charge you for something that should be free.

Currently even the person checking if a document/contract is sealed or code is authentic has to also be inside the same Adobe walled garden too. Verification, the part that should be free is the part everyone charges for. Thats the shape Let's Encrypt fixed for TLS, and I wanted the same thing for documents and files.

The core idea therefore needed to go a bit beyond e signatures and i created an open standard (SEAL), plus free tools that implement it.

When you seal a file, three independent things happen.

1. it gets a signature from a certificate authority, chaining to a public root. 2. its record is appended to an RFC 6962 transparency log. and 3. its SHA256 is timestamped on a public blockchain (Bitcoin) via OpenTimestamps. Those three give you integrity, transparency and a timestamped proof. And importantly, none of those depend on Let's Seal and none are gated.

title: Show HN: Justif – Knuth-Plass justification and microtypography for the web
body:
Justif is a drop-in JavaScript library that progressively enhances web pages to TeX-level text justification. Installation is a single <script> line, standard text and accessibility affordances are unchanged, and users with JS disabled get native browser rendering.

I made justif because I've long been a fan of justified text. I think it looks clean and elegant, and makes reading more enjoyable. But bad justification is the opposite, with gaping spaces that distract me to the point of making the text near unreadable.

Browsers have got better recently at handling justified text [0][1], but still use suboptimal greedy algorithms for the most part, and are not near that TeX/InDesign level of quality that I crave. `text-wrap: pretty` exists but is far from a panacea, as you can see for yourself in the demo.

 Problem 1 : Search is unreliable: Using Facebook's built-in search within the group doesn't return all posts from a given year. Some posts are omitted for no apparent reason, even when filtering by date. 
 Problem 2 : Scrolling crashes: Manually scrolling back through the group's history works up to a point, but once I reach posts from around 2022, the browser tab/app consistently crashes before I can get further back. 
 Constraint: The posts don't share consistent keywords or phrasing, so text-based search isn't a reliable filter. Filtering by month/year seems like the only practical approach, but I can't get it to work reliably.
What I'm looking for: 
 A reliable method or tool to filter/export Facebook group posts by date range
Any way to export or archive a group's full post history (browser extension, API, third-party tool, etc.) 
 A workaround for the crashing when scrolling through several years of content 
 Has anyone dealt with this before, and what worked for you?

title: 'Action Required' Sign in to Google Photos with your Google Account to keep your photos & videos
body:
I get these emails frequently with subject line "[Action Required] Sign in to Google Photos with your Google Account to keep your photos & videos". Every time it's from a different email. It seems to  be click bait and a security issue but there is no CVE related to it. 
 The email message contains 
 
 This is a copy of a security alert sent to <some_username@gmail.com>.
<myactualemail@gmail.com> is the recovery email for this account. If
you don't recognize this account, remove it. 
 
 But my email shouldn't be the recovery email of any of these accounts. 
 If anyone thinks all of a sudden, 50 different people are sharing photos with me, that's not normal. Does someone understand what this is? And why is Google not doing anything about this when their platform is being abused?

 ="Players with open reports: "& countif(D3:D, "true") 
It always returns 0.

title: How to stop Outlook capitalizing small letters?
body: The web Outlook (used in the Office 365 package by our university) automatically capitalizes anything on a new line or after a full stop, for example after an abbreviation. This is driving me mad and causes numerous inadvertent mistakes. Is there any way to stop this? I tried to disable all automatic corrections I was able to find. It is 100% harmful, I can capitalize the intended letters on my own.

title: How to have text float around an image with a margin in README.md on GitLab's repository / branch view?
body:
I am using a selfhosted GitLab CE 19.0.2. 
 I want text to float around an image in a project  README.md  like HTML  float: left , and a spacing between image and text (like  margin  or  padding ) when it is rendered on GitLab's branch view. 
 I tried: 
 
  <img align="left">   text floats, but no margin. text sticks at the edge of the image 
 Inline CSS  style="float:left; margin-right:12px"   does nothing; GitLab's sanitizer strips style from .  hspace   vspace  seemingly survive but too render no visible margin 
 Transparent-padding workaround I baked a transparent strip into the image (PNG/WebP alpha) to force a padding inside the image itself on its right and bottom. Yet while it renders the image still, this broke the float completly. It renders as if I had no float set to begin with. 
 
 Esp. the 3rd option I thought would work: 
  <img src="docs/_img/my_image_having_baked_in_transparent_margin.webp" align="left" width="400"> The text I expect to float.
<br clear="all">
  
 
 This is how my trials render: 
   
 How to get an image to have text float around while still having a margin visible?

title: How do I search Facebook Marketplace for recent trending sold items?
body: How do I search Facebook Marketplace for recent trending sold items? Trying to see if there’s a way to search somewhere on Facebook marketplace or elsewhere for trending items that have been selling within the last month or two. More so, items that are trending within a set distance limit. Something kind of like what you can do on eBay where you can search an item and then filter for “sold” items within the last 90 days.

title: How to disconnect a family account
body:
For home automation, I created a new Google account (so it could be left with the home when I move out).  For Date of Birth, I put in the move in date (so I would remember it). 
 Because it thinks I am 2 years old, the account is supervised by my main account. 
 The problem is that its a lot of hassle to enrol all the devices. 
 How can I stop the supervision? 
  Note I have already gone in and changed the date of birth, but the account is still supervised.
